provenance.instrument: Upper Uwchlan Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 200 Zoning, Ord. No. 89-06 of 6-7-1989, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 UP2148, Township of Upper Uwchlan, Chester County. Chapter 200 Zoning was adopted 6-7-1989 by Ord. No. 89-06 and amended many times, most recently by Ord. No. 2026-03 (8-17-2026), which is folded into the definitions and the parking section. 200-62 was last amended by Ord. No. 2025-05 (10-20-2025). The former conversion of dwellings section (200-63) was repealed by Ord. No. 2024-01 (7-15-2024). New Laws: none. Each district article sets its uses and figures in text. The chapter page lists no attachments
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360: 'Includes legislation through 08-17-2026.' New Laws: none
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit listing. The nearest rule is a use accessory to a single-family dwelling: 'quarters for guests and for servants or tenants, employed on the premises' (200-62B(1)). R-1 permits 'Customary residential accessory uses', and R-2, R-3 and R-4 permit any accessory use permitted in R-1 (200-13E, 200-17C, 200-21C, 200-27C)

Where the quarters are in a building detached from the house, the lot needs the district's minimum lot area times the number of separate housekeeping units on the lot. For a house and one detached unit that is twice the minimum: 4 acres in R-1, 2 acres in R-2, 60,000 sq ft in R-3 and 40,000 sq ft in R-4 with central sewer and public water (200-62B(1), 200-14A, 200-18A, 200-22A, 200-28A)
'The rental or leasing of any of such quarters shall not be permitted' (200-62B(1)). A family includes 'domestic servants or gratuitous guests' living in a common household (200-7)

The code does not say whether such quarters may have their own kitchen. A dwelling unit has 'its own permanently installed cooking and sanitary facilities' (200-7). A second dwelling unit inside the house would make it a two-family detached dwelling (duplex), which only R-3 and R-4 permit (200-21A, 200-27A)

A two-family detached dwelling (duplex, one unit over the other) is by right in R-3 and R-4, at 20,000 sq ft per unit in R-3 and 15,000 sq ft per unit in R-4, with central sewer and public water (200-22A(2), 200-28A(2), 200-23A)

The former section on conversion of dwellings (200-63) was repealed by Ord. No. 2024-01. The parking table still lists 'Accessory apartments for family members' at 1.0 space, 'Apartment in combination with a business' and 'Residential conversions' (200-73G(2)), but the chapter as read defines and lists none of them
Accessory buildings may not stand in the front yard and may not be taller than 25 ft (200-14E, F, 200-18E, F, 200-22E, F, 200-28E, F)
On a lot under two acres, lot area does not count land in the Flood Hazard District, rights-of-way and easements, or slopes over 25% (200-7 'Lot area')
A building may be constructed on a nonconforming lot of record. Yards that cannot be met need a special exception, and contiguous nonconforming lots in common ownership count as one lot (200-104A)
No section read bars a use variance or gives a path for uses the code does not list. Variances need the findings of 200-126I
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Upper Uwchlan Township, Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360, one page at a time, on 2026-11-16, mostly in print view. Read: 200-7 (definitions from the start through 'Municipal use'), Articles IV to VIII (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, C-1), 200-62, 200-63, 200-73, 200-104, 200-126 and the New Laws page. Not read: Articles X to XII (C-3, LI, PI), the definitions after 'Municipal use', 200-64 to 200-72.4 (including 200-71 planned residential development and 200-72.1 adaptive reuse for historic preservation), the rest of Article XV, Articles XVI to XVIII (including the Steep Slope Conservation District), Article XIX, the rest of Article XX, Article XXI and Chapter 82 (floodplain). The code search was run for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, family member, living quarters, ECHO, guest house, tenant house, caretaker, conversion, second dwelling, carriage house, granny, accessory suite and relative. Building coverage counts accessory buildings and lot coverage is impervious cover (200-7). A lot holds one principal building except for multifamily and multiuse commercial and industrial developments (200-7 'Lot').

status.note: Quarters only for guests, or for servants or tenants employed on the premises, and they may not be rented or leased. The code's family includes 'domestic servants or gratuitous guests'. Allowed as a customary residential accessory use in R-1 to R-4

status_outside.note: C-1 permits no house by right and only customary commercial accessory uses. C-3, LI and PI were not read

path.note: A customary residential accessory use, so a zoning permit. No hearing is named

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (duplex)
value.conditions: 'Two dwelling units, each accommodating one family, which are located one over the other with the building having two side yards' (200-7). By right in R-3 and R-4 (200-21A(2), 200-27A). 20,000 sq ft per unit in R-3 and 15,000 sq ft per unit in R-4, average aggregate width 100 ft (R-3) or 75 ft (R-4) for the two units, front 50 ft, sides 25 ft, rear 40 ft (200-22, 200-28). Centralized sewer and public water are required (200-23A, 200-29). Parking 3 spaces for each single-family home (200-73G(2))
value.note: Lot figures are per unit, so a duplex needs twice the figure. The units are one over the other. Without central sewer and public water, 200-23A allows one unit per gross acre

historic_bypass.note: No historic ADU path found in the sections read. 200-72.1 (adaptive reuse for historic preservation) was not read

districts_read_no_listing.note: C-1 permits offices, shops, restaurants and similar uses, mixed-use dwellings by conditional use, and customary commercial accessory uses

value.condition: The quarters are for guests, or for servants or tenants employed on the premises. 'The rental or leasing of any of such quarters shall not be permitted.'
Quarters in a detached building need the district minimum times the number of housekeeping units on the lot. In R-1 that is 4 acres for the house and one unit
Quarters in a detached building need the district minimum times the number of housekeeping units on the lot. In R-2 that is 2 acres for the house and one unit

Quarters in a detached building need the district minimum times the number of housekeeping units on the lot. In R-3 that is 60,000 sq ft for the house and one unit, or 2 acres where the lot lacks central sewer or public water and the R-2 figures apply

Quarters in a detached building need the district minimum times the number of housekeeping units on the lot. In R-4 that is 40,000 sq ft for the house and one unit, or 2 acres where the lot lacks central sewer or public water and the R-2 figures apply

The code does not say whether the quarters may have their own kitchen. A second dwelling unit with its own cooking facilities inside the house would make it a two-family detached dwelling, permitted only in R-3 and R-4.
